abstract: Can a prescribed expanding Collatz prefix retain its inverse-minimum protection while admitting a substantially smaller source at a later common future? We prove a uniform deterministic bound for the established counted-pair dynamics: from every live state $(s,D)$, an explicitly constructible absorbing label word has length at most $2s+3\lfloor s/2\rfloor-\operatorname{popcount}(\lfloor s/2\rfloor)+7\operatorname{bitlength}(|D|+3^s)+3$. The proof combines the known valuation rule with an exact sum over levels and a magnitude budget. Exact binary cylinders realize the chosen word. Applying the bound to the denominator-139 rational shadow with accelerated exponent period $(1,2,1,2,1,2,2)$ gives infinitely many positive odd multiples of three $n$ with smaller odd multiples of three $b<n^{1-1/2048}$. Their trajectories meet with equal total odd counts while every nonempty original prefix through the meeting exceeds $n$. The original sources retain unbounded prefixes covered by the prior inverse-minimum theorem. Every sufficiently large octave $[X,2X)$ contains at least $\sqrt X/7$ such certificates with the weaker bound $b<n^{1-1/8192}$, protected prefix length proportional to $\log X$, and meeting within $\tfrac12\log_2X+1$ shortcut steps. Earlier constructions have stronger numerical power exponents; the contribution is the general linear word bound and its simultaneous protected-prefix, count, and interval guarantees. Exact finite audits support the arithmetic implementation, with long-prefix replay scope stated explicitly. These sparse certificates do not cover every source or prove the Collatz conjecture.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Linear absorbing words and protected smaller-source certificates for Collatz
